references.text: Jesus' parallel teaching in the Sermon on the Mount: "Do not judge, so that you will not be judged! For with the judgment you make, you yourselves will be judged." This is the closest parallel to Luke 6:37.
Paul warns against judging others, because whoever judges does the same themselves: "Therefore you have no excuse, you human being who judges." The theme of not judging others is central.
Paul exhorts believers in Rome not to judge their brother or look down on him, for we will all stand before God's judgment seat. This expands on the principle of not judging from Luke 6:37.

James exhorts: "Do not speak evil against one another, brothers and sisters. Whoever slanders a brother or judges his brother, slanders the law and judges the law." The same principle of not judging each other.
"For judgment is merciless to anyone who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment." This is linked to the promise in Luke 6:37 that whoever forgives will be forgiven.

Jesus teaches that if we forgive others, our heavenly Father will forgive us, but if we do not forgive, neither will the Father forgive us. This supports "Forgive, and you will be forgiven" in Luke 6:37.
The parable of the unforgiving servant illustrates the principle that whoever does not forgive others will not themselves be forgiven. This expands on the final part of Luke 6:37 about forgiving.
Paul exhorts: "Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving each other, just as God in Christ forgave you." The theme of forgiveness from Luke 6:37 is expanded here.
"Bear with one another and forgive each other if one has a complaint against another. As the Lord has forgiven you, so also you must forgive." A direct parallel to the call to forgive in Luke 6:37.
Jesus says that when praying, one must forgive if they have something against someone, so that the heavenly Father will also forgive their sins. A parallel principle of forgiveness as in Luke 6:37.
Paul says: "Therefore do not judge anything before the time, before the Lord comes. He will bring to light what is hidden in darkness." An exhortation against judging that corresponds with Luke 6:37.

"Do not act unjustly when you judge. You shall not favor the poor or show partiality to the powerful. You shall judge your neighbor fairly." Old Testament background for righteous judgment and the warning against condemnation.
